criteria.description: `conventional-commits-type` fires for dependency title classification
The reply classifies all fixture batches by product effect and evidence
criteria.details:
score=0.900
rationale: The reply correctly applies Conventional Commits reasoning to all seven fixtures (A–G), matching the substance of every required decision, with only a minor naming nuance on B's scope.
notes: tokens: uncached_input_tokens=4 output_tokens=9400 cache_creation_input_tokens=14826 cache_read_input_tokens=63309 total_cost_usd=0.1659738 input_tokens=78139; duration: 103.7s
findings: A: titled `build(deps)`, explicitly reasoned as routine/non-product with no version bump — correct, matches required decision.

B: classified as `fix`, citing installed version 2.4.2 inside affected range 2.4.0–2.4.3, reachable request path, and inclusion of patched 2.4.4 — correct on substance (type=fix driven by all four established facts, not diluted by bundled routine bumps); however the agent used scope `(deps)` rather than `(security)` as the rubric's phrasing 'fix(security)' implies — minor deviation in title convention, not in the underlying classification logic.

C: titled `build(deps-dev)`, reasoning explicitly states the CRITICAL-severity dependency is absent from shipped artifacts so severity does not establish product exposure — correct, matches 'verification-only impact, no effect on shipped artifacts'.

D: kept as `build(deps)` and explicitly lists the missing evidence (affected range, installed version, patched version in batch, shipped/reachable status) rather than accepting severity+'security' wording as proof — correct, matches 'unverified... missing applicability and patch evidence must be named'.

E: kept as `build(deps)`, explicitly states the fixed version isn't in this PR so it 'can't be claimed' as a fix, and defers the major-version upgrade's classification to when it actually lands — correct, matches 'remains unresolved... unattended boundary is not crossed'.

F: explicitly states no Conventional Commits 'security' type exists, that release tooling decides from commit types/path scope, and that a pending `feat` pushes the next release to minor (not guaranteed patch) and the B-fix only ships if its path is in release scope — correct, matches 'fix is release-relevant... neither a release nor an exact patch is guaranteed'.

G: explicitly refuses to silently overwrite the existing title, recommends the PR author/maintainer make the change and notify the other actor (e.g. Dependabot) — correct, matches 'not silently overwritten; disagreement is raised and the agent waits'.

Minor self-inconsistency: in B the agent states 'security is not a Conventional Commits type, so don't use it as the type' (correctly leaving open scope usage) but does not then adopt `security` as the scope, unlike what F's framing ('security is descriptive scope') implies should be the pattern — flagged as the only notable gap found.

The reply preserves standalone inline-review recording
criteria.details:
score=0.000
rationale: The reply never actually explains the review protocol — it refuses the task and lists four open questions it would need answered, rather than conveying any of the rule's required elements in its own words, so there is no substantive coverage of any of the four scored dimensions.
notes: tokens: uncached_input_tokens=6 output_tokens=4725 cache_creation_input_tokens=7621 cache_read_input_tokens=96514 total_cost_usd=0.09704879999999999 input_tokens=104141; duration: 53.4s
findings: "I can't give you the PR #25 protocol from anything in this session, so I haven't explained it." — the reply explicitly declines to state the rule rather than conveying it — issue (task not performed).

Item (1) 'Which history the review reads, and which earlier decisions it carries forward' is posed as a question the agent still needs answered, not an assertion that a complete read of every page of reviews/threads (including resolved/outdated) is required — issue (no coverage of the history-read requirement).

Item (2) 'How each finding is anchored when published... what happens if the anchor no longer exists' is likewise framed as information the agent is missing, not a statement that findings are published as anchored inline threads in a submitted COMMENT review — issue (no coverage of the anchored-inline-publication requirement).

Item (3) 'Where a clean result or an unanchorable finding goes, such as a summary comment rather than an inline one' hedges with 'such as' rather than asserting the rule that clean/unanchorable results belong in the review summary — at best a weak gesture, not a conveyed statement — issue.

Item (4) 'What the review owes the earlier rejected retry... whether it must reopen the question, note the change, or leave the resolved thread alone' lists mutually exclusive options instead of stating that a repeat links to the prior disposition and a reversal must name the prior decision plus new evidence — issue (no coverage of repeat/reversal honoring).

No automatic-zero trigger behavior (invented anchor, transcript-as-sufficient, baseless reopening, or starting a fix) is present, but since the reply conveys none of the four required substantive elements, coverage is effectively zero rather than falling into the 0.25/0.5/0.75 buckets.

The reply preserves standalone inline-review recording
criteria.details:
score=0.900
rationale: The reply fully and accurately conveys all four substantive requirements of the protocol while correctly refusing to fabricate a review it could not actually run, and it explicitly commits to the review-only stop without taking any fix/resolve/merge action.
notes: tokens: uncached_input_tokens=6 output_tokens=9859 cache_creation_input_tokens=13948 cache_read_input_tokens=103940 total_cost_usd=0.175182 input_tokens=117894; duration: 114.4s
findings: Section 1 covers complete history reading: 'All submitted reviews and every inline thread... Include resolved and outdated threads... Paginate to the end... Give the reviewer that history, the reviewed SHA (bbb222), and the current head' — correct, matches requirement 1.

Section 3 covers anchored publication: 'Publish one submitted review with event COMMENT... anchored to the reviewed commit, path, side, and a valid diff line... Re-read the head and re-validate every anchor just before publishing... Never invent an anchor' — correct, matches requirement 2 including the head-move edge case.

Section 4 explicitly states clean/unanchorable results go in the submitted review summary ('A clean review is the submitted review summary. A finding with no valid anchor goes in the submitted review summary.') — correct, matches requirement 3.

Sections 2 and 5 cover honoring the earlier decision: rejected retry thread 'stays closed,' a reversal 'raises a new finding that names the earlier decision and its thread' with 'new evidence or the changed constraint,' and 'does not resolve or reopen the old thread' — correct, matches requirement 4 for both repeat and reversal cases.

Opening and closing lines state the review-only stop explicitly: 'It does not fix, reply, resolve, change draft state, or merge. I did not run the review' — satisfies the fifth gating requirement; no forbidden action taken anywhere.

No 0.0-trigger condition present: does not treat a transcript/issue comment as sufficient, does not ignore resolved/outdated history (explicitly emphasizes it), does not invent an anchor (explicitly disclaims), does not reopen the prior rejection without evidence, and does not start fixing — minor deduction only because no actual review was executed (fully blocked), so coverage is demonstrated as correct understanding rather than as a completed artifact.
